front: How does interactive video differ from a buffered download?
back: Interactive media needs timely delivery; buffering and retransmission may make file transfer more tolerant of delay. Neither application has unlimited tolerance for loss or poor throughput.

front: Where is the three-bit CoS/PCP field?
back: In an IEEE 802.1Q tag, with values 0–7. An untagged Ethernet frame has no PCP field, but its IP packet may carry DSCP.

front: How are the IP service field's eight bits divided?
back: Six bits carry DSCP (0–63); two carry ECN. This applies to the IPv4 DS field and IPv6 Traffic Class interpretation.

front: Which decimal DSCP is recommended for EF?
back: 46. EF is commonly used for voice media, but the mark needs a corresponding policy at each hop; it does not create an end-to-end reservation.

front: Calculate AFxy and interpret its two digits.
back: DSCP = 8x + 2y. x is AF class 1–4; y is drop precedence 1–3. Higher y means greater discard eligibility within that AF class.

front: Must AF41 receive more bandwidth than AF21?
back: No. AF class labels are not a universal bandwidth ranking. Resources and mappings depend on the configured policy.

front: What is a QoS trust boundary?
back: Where the network decides whether incoming markings may be used as policy input. Validate untrusted endpoint markings before granting preferred service.
match-all requires every configured criterion (AND); match-any requires at least one (OR). Classification is separate from a policy action.

front: What can unconstrained strict priority do to other queues?
back: Sustained priority traffic can starve lower-priority traffic. Suitable rate control and capacity planning protect other service classes.

front: CBWFQ bandwidth versus classic IOS LLQ priority?
back: bandwidth supplies a minimum share during congestion. priority also gives priority scheduling, with a congestion-time rate/burst limit in the classic IOS example.
Tail drop acts when a queue is full. WRED can act probabilistically earlier and differentiate drop behavior by marking; it is queue management, not scheduling.
A policer meters then applies transmit/drop/remark actions without queuing excess traffic to wait. A shaper delays traffic in a finite buffer; overflow can still drop.

front: Does shaping change physical Ethernet speed?
back: No. Frames still transmit at the physical rate; the shaper regulates departure timing. Its rate and burst accounting determine the resulting traffic profile.
Classification identifies a traffic category. Marking writes a value that this or another device can use as policy input.
Delay is delivery time; jitter is variation in that delay. The same average delay can hide very different variation.
The treatment a device gives a traffic aggregate at one hop. A good local policy does not establish the treatment at every later hop.

front: Why compare policy counters before and after a known test?
back: Their change relates to the interval. A nonzero cumulative value may belong to older traffic or the opposite direction.
